title: Physical and chemical change
caption: Melting ice is a physical change: the same H₂O molecules, now free to move. Burning hydrogen is a chemical change: atoms rearrange into a new substance, 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. In both, every atom is still there.
alt: Top: ice as an ordered grid of water molecules becoming liquid water, the same molecules disordered. Bottom: hydrogen and oxygen molecules becoming water molecules.
description: Ice: water molecules in a regular arrangement.
Water: the same nine molecules, close together but disordered.
Hydrogen and oxygen: four H₂ and two O₂ molecules.
After burning: four H₂O molecules, the same atoms rearranged.
